## VOCABULARY
Each helper is `name(g, ...)`, writes via `g.set` and the `B.*` block helpers, and returns the cells it wrote. Coordinates are corner-origin unless stated. Shares of ~10 are written at once by separate sessions, in this order.

**Frame and walls**
1. `beamRun(g, axis, a0, a1, fixed, y, fixed2)` — a horizontal `stripped_spruce_wood` run with `axis: x|z`, from a0 to a1 at the given other coordinates. E.g. sill `beamRun(g,"x",6,16,8,6)` (z=8, y=6).
2. `postRun(g, x, y0, y1, z)` — vertical `stripped_spruce_log` axis y, y0..y1.

4. `fachwerkWall(g, axis, fixed, a0, a1, y0, y1, posts[], windows[], braced[])` — composes 1–3: posts at `posts`, sill at y0, breast rail at y0+1, head plate at y1, daub between, `windows` = list of [a0,a1,ya,yb] left unset, `braced` = panel indices that get `mannBrace`. input.summary:
parts/yard.mjs builds the back and side yard ground (grass with podzol flecks, coarse dirt at tree feet), dirt paths from the back door, wing door and west gate, and the yard fence with gates at (1,1,20) and (23,1,16).
Also the bench at x=2..4 z=10, woodpile x=7..10 z=24..25, wheat patch x=2..5 z=24..28, spruces at (2,15) and (3,29), and the prop yard x=12..15 z=24..26.
make.sh writes a whole build.nbt; part 5 shows 464 placed with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE lines; the check reports 0 floating and 0 unsupported blocks, and the walk is end-to-end true.
left: Street, kerb and sidewalk are not built by this part: the plan's element 'Street + sidewalk' is ticked-open and belongs to part 1 (shell) unless the shell leaves it out.
Farmland under the wheat has no water block within 4 cells, so it will dry back to dirt; the plan has no water source and I did not add one off-spec.
The woodpile (x=7..10, z=24..25) sits across the back-door path at x=8; the walk goes around it via x=6 or x=11, so it is passable but the path is hidden under the stack.
The west gate (1,1,20) opens onto the lot edge at x=0, and the east gate (23,1,16) opens onto nothing (x=23 is the last lot column). Both match the plan's coordinates but read as gates to nowhere.
Mehlboden is unreachable in the walk check; that is the flour-loft room (room 6), not this part.

waste.what: Ground mix of grass and podzol over the yard and both side strips was done as three scatterBlend calls, and the coarse-dirt tree feet as hand-written 3x3 fills.
waste.cost: about 5 minutes of picking the regions and writing fills by hand; each tree foot was a separate fill.
waste.tool: a groundMix(g, box, {base, flecks:[[block, ratio]]}) helper that blends several materials in one call and a treeFoot(g, x, z, radius) helper for coarse dirt round a trunk.

waste.what: Dirt paths were coordinated by hand as straight fills (back door to fence, wing door east, west gate up the lot edge), with no widening at the ends.
waste.cost: 3 fills, plus a check by eye that the paths meet the doors and gates.
waste.tool: a path(g, [[x,z],...], {block, width}) polyline helper that lays dirt_path along the door-to-gate-to-street route and widens it at the ends.

waste.what: Checking that the walk still reaches the entrance and that the gates land on the path took a render and a zoom by eye.
waste.cost: 2 renders and a zoom, judged by eye.
waste.tool: a walk check that reports which path cells are reached from each door, so path and gate alignment can be read as a verdict rather than from a picture.
